recommendations.regimenLabel: First-line — stop ACEi, protect airway, empirical anaphylaxis therapy if any doubt
steps: Assess and protect the AIRWAY early — low threshold for senior anaesthetic/ENT involvement and early intubation.
Bradykinin-mediated angioedema responds poorly to adrenaline/steroids/antihistamines, but give them if any doubt about anaphylaxis.
Hereditary angioedema: specific therapy (C1-esterase-inhibitor concentrate, icatibant).
Observe for delayed/progressive swelling; avoid ACEi/ARB in future.

drugRefs.regimenLabel: IM adrenaline (only if anaphylaxis cannot be excluded)
drugRefs.why: Bradykinin-mediated angioedema responds poorly, but give empirically when an allergic/anaphylactic mechanism cannot be excluded — do not withhold if in doubt.
Adjunct only if a histaminergic/allergic component is suspected; ineffective for pure bradykinin-mediated swelling.
Only useful if a histaminergic component is present; not effective for bradykinin-mediated angioedema.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Urticaria, Angioedema and Allergic Rhinitis (Ch. 363)
WAO/EAACI Guideline for the Management of Hereditary Angioedema

drugRefs.freq: single dose; may repeat after 6 h (max 3 doses/24 h)
drugRefs.why: Directly antagonises bradykinin; used for hereditary angioedema attacks and considered off-label in severe ACEi-induced angioedema.
Replaces deficient/consumed C1-inhibitor in hereditary/acquired angioedema, restraining bradykinin generation.

refs: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine, 22e — Urticaria, Angioedema and Allergic Rhinitis (Ch. 363)
WAO/EAACI Guideline for the Management of Hereditary Angioedema

confirm: Non-pitting swelling of lips/tongue/face/airway WITHOUT urticaria; ACE-inhibitor or hereditary (bradykinin-mediated). Assess airway.
